item.title: Zero margins: Model shows Europe’s long odds in a Baltic war
item.description: As Washington increasingly adopts a more transactional approach to defence in Europe, the threat to those states on the border with Russia increases. Simulations suggest that while Europe remains more powerful, it may simply be unable to overcome internal differences in time to stop Moscow’s plans. item.title: The western delusion of the Russian opposition
item.description: Western institutions treat exiled Russian opposition figures as democratic alternatives to Putin. In reality, they lack legitimacy, are deeply divided, and often prioritize Russian victimhood over Ukrainian suffering. Artykuł The western delusion of the Russian opposition pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: Ukraine’s fields, the EU border
item.description: Ukraine’s agricultural industry has faced a variety of challenges since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion. While farmers have fought hard to maintain production, its export has caused friction with allies in the West. It is clear that agriculture will remain a key issue in ongoing talks over the country’s potential integration. Artykuł Ukraine’s fields, the EU border pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: America embraces imperialism and ditches Europe
item.description: In 2025, America abandoned Ukraine and Europe to Russia and chose the imperial past as a future. It is a turning point. Washington nodded eagerly in agreement with Moscow’s insistence on dividing the world into 19th-century-style spheres of influence. AI rapidly replaces hydrocarbons as the main source of wealth and influence. Only states with stockpiles of nuclear weapons remain genuinely sovereign. Artykuł America embraces imperialism and ditches Europe pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: The Kremlin’s poker face
item.description: The logic underpinning the hand that Moscow picks for itself can only lead in certain directions. With de-escalation seen as a loss in and of itself, it is only logical for the Kremlin to continue an escalatory approach in 2026. Artykuł The Kremlin’s poker face pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: Reframing Ukraine: A review of Olga Khomenko’s The Faraway Sky of Kyiv: Ukrainians in the War
item.description: Writing has become a powerful weapon for Ukrainians contending with Russia’s ongoing invasion. This is particularly clear with regards to Olga Khomenko’s new work, which forges novel connections between Ukraine and the world during this difficult time. item.title: Western geopolitics and Balkan corruption: How US and EU justice reform efforts fuelled power centralization and failed justice
item.description: The prospects for European integration in the Western Balkans remain difficult to measure. While regional capitals continue their attempts to show progress in various fields, related actions often present only a facade of reform. This is particularly true in the highly contentious spheres of the rule of law and corruption. Artykuł Western geopolitics and Balkan corruption: How US and EU justice reform efforts fuelled power centralization and failed justice pochodzi z serwisu New Eastern Europe.

item.title: Shoring up the Balkans: NATO infrastructure and a warning for democracy
item.description: Recent shifts in US foreign policy are placing the Western Balkans in a difficult position. While internal issues are challenging a delicate peace, outside forces are only exacerbating these issues. It now falls to the European Union to provide a clear path forward amidst such uncertainty. item.title: Gold in the age of sanctions: How the Russia-Ukraine war reshaped the global bullion market
item.description: Gold is experiencing something of a resurgence in the current geopolitical climate. Ongoing issues such as Russia-Ukraine conflict have highlighted how currency can be linked to government action, inspiring investment in a commodity thought to escape such restrictions.
